title: Fox & Goose Public House
venue_description:
Historic English-Style Pub and Music Venue

Located within the Fuller Building - Fox & Goose Public House opened in 1975 and has become a beloved Sacramento institution. The venue was founded by Bill and Denise Dalton - who named it after Bill's hometown pub in Hebden Bridge - Yorkshire - England. The building itself dates to 1913 - creating an authentic old-factory-brick atmosphere that perfectly complements the traditional English pub experience.

Live Music Legacy

Fox & Goose hosts live music five nights per week - with Monday's open mic night serving as Sacramento's longest-running music open mic - operating continuously for over 30 years. Hosted by Dave Baldwin - the open mic uses a lottery system for performance order - ensuring fairness while maintaining the excitement of the draw. Musicians perform three songs for 15 minutes - and a featured artist closes each evening. The show runs until everyone who wants to play has performed - no matter how late. Weekend performances feature diverse bands across multiple genres - while Tuesday evenings are dedicated to Pub Quiz trivia night.

Dining and Drinks

The pub serves breakfast - lunch - and dinner with a menu featuring traditional English fare including fish and chips - bangers and mash - corned beef hash - smoked salmon - and their famous olallieberry scones. American classics like omelets - waffles - pancakes - and French toast round out the breakfast offerings. The bar features a carefully curated selection of wines - beers - and cocktails. Many regulars visit for the warm - welcoming atmosphere that makes Fox & Goose feel like a second home.

Community Hub

The venue's intimate layout creates interesting sight lines throughout the historic building - though many seats do face the performance area. The old brick walls and vintage architecture add character to every event. Fox & Goose has evolved from a simple pub into a true community gathering place where artists - regulars - and newcomers all find common ground. The venue celebrated its 50th anniversary in January 2025 - marking half a century of serving Sacramento's Midtown neighborhood with authentic hospitality and quality entertainment.

title: Old Ironsides
venue_description:
Sacramento's Oldest Bar and Historic Music Venue

Old Ironsides holds the distinguished honor of being Sacramento's oldest continuously operating bar - established in 1934 when William Bill Bordisso obtained the first liquor license issued in Sacramento County after the end of Prohibition in 1933. For 88 years - the venue was family-owned and operated by the Bordisso/Kanelos family before being sold in 2022 to Bret Bair and Eric Rushing - the founders of Ace of Spades and former owners of Holy Diver.

Evolution into Music Venue

In the 1990s - the next generation of the Kanelos family transformed Old Ironsides from a traditional neighborhood bar into one of Sacramento's premier small-scale music venues. The 150-person capacity room features a stage in the back room with excellent acoustics created by the building's original brick walls. The venue quickly became legendary for hosting touring acts across rock - indie - punk - metal - and alternative genres alongside the best local musicians. Wednesday night open mic has become a staple event - while the LIPSTICK indie rock dance party - hosted by Shaun Slaughter and Roger Carpio - has drawn lines around the building monthly for over 20 years.

Live Music Programming

Old Ironsides hosts live music Thursday through Saturday nights - with some shows extending into early Sunday morning. The venue is known for booking diverse acts and providing excellent sound quality in an intimate setting. Tuesday nights feature karaoke - creating a full week of programming for music lovers. The back room stage area transforms from a dining space during lunch hours into a packed music venue by night - maintaining the authentic dive bar character while delivering professional-quality performances.

Historic Significance

The building's history as a Prohibition-era establishment is evident throughout the space. In earlier decades - Old Ironsides operated a bottle shop where politicians - judges - and state workers would gather for two or three martini lunches. The venue has witnessed nearly a century of Sacramento's evolution - from its days as a neighborhood watering hole to its current status as a beloved music institution. The family atmosphere persists even under new ownership - with long-time staff members maintaining the welcoming vibe that has defined Old Ironsides for generations.

title: Torch Club
venue_description:
Sacramento's Premiere Blues Club Since 1934

Established in 1934 - the same year Prohibition ended - Torch Club stands as one of Sacramento's oldest and most beloved music venues. For over 85 years - this intimate club has served as the undisputed home for blues music in Sacramento - earning a reputation that extends throughout California and beyond. The 75-100 person capacity creates an up-close - personal experience where audiences connect directly with performers in an authentic blues club atmosphere.

Blues Heritage and Programming

Torch Club showcases live music Wednesday through Sunday - with performances often extending to Sunday afternoons. The venue has hosted blues legends including Terry Hanck - Janiva Magness - The Delgado Brothers - Shane Dwight - Mark Hummel - Mick Martin & the Blues Rockers - Daniel Castro - Popa Chubby - and Chris Cain alongside Sacramento's finest local musicians. House bands maintain the club's authentic tradition - including The Lew Fratis Trio - Jimmy Pailer & the Prophets - Aaron King Trio - Stacie Eakes and the Superfreaks - and Mind X.

Open Mic and Jam Sessions

Wednesday evenings from 6:00-8:00 PM feature the popular semi-acoustic open mic - hosted by Todd Perez. Musicians arrive early to claim their preferred time slots on a first-come - first-served basis. Performers play 2-3 songs - and the host provides board mix recordings for those who bring flash drives - allowing musicians to review and share their performances. Sunday afternoons are reserved for blues jam sessions where musicians gather to improvise and collaborate - creating spontaneous musical moments that embody the blues tradition.

Venue Character and Atmosphere

The club's intimate brick-walled space features excellent acoustics that performers and audiences consistently praise. A welcoming dance floor invites movement - while the bar serves quality drinks at reasonable prices. The venue maintains a laid-back atmosphere where the music always takes center stage. Despite being one of Sacramento's oldest establishments - Torch Club feels vibrant and alive - bridging the gap between preserving blues heritage and nurturing new generations of musicians. The club's commitment to showcasing both local and national acts across blues - jazz - funk - country - and reggae has made it essential to Sacramento's music ecosystem.

title: Kupros Craft House
venue_description:
Midtown's Premier Craft Bar in a Historic Craftsman Home

Kupros Craft House occupies a beautifully preserved 1910 two-story Craftsman building in the heart of Midtown Sacramento. The venue's Victorian decor - polished wood accents - and stunning stained glass fixtures create a warm - inviting atmosphere that feels like a comfortable second home to the many regulars who gather here. The historic architecture includes unique features like the only upstairs balcony in Midtown and a spacious front porch - perfect for enjoying Sacramento's mild climate.

Craft Beverages and Elevated Cuisine

Kupros features an extensive selection of craft beers and hand-crafted cocktails that showcase local and regional breweries. The bar staff takes pride in helping guests discover new favorites from the rotating tap list. The kitchen serves elevated bar classics made with fresh local ingredients - focusing on quality and creative preparations. Popular menu items include buffalo cauliflower bites with excellent dipping sauce - grilled chicken sandwiches - blackened mahi mahi burgers with Caesar salad - and the classic Cobb salad. Weekend brunch draws crowds for generous mimosa pitchers - fluffy French toast - and hearty breakfast plates.

Community Events and Entertainment

Tuesday evenings feature open mic nights that welcome musicians - comedians - and poets in a relaxed - supportive atmosphere. Sign-ups begin at 7:30 PM - and the venue maintains an all-ages policy until 10 PM - making it accessible to younger performers and families. The stage is tucked in the back corner - adding ambient music to the bar while allowing those not specifically attending for performances to enjoy their meals and conversations. Trivia nights and occasional live music performances fill out the weekly calendar of events.

Atmosphere and Character

The repurposed Craftsman home creates multiple distinct spaces - from the main dining area with its mix of tables and booths to the upstairs balcony offering a unique vantage point. The outdoor patio extends the usable space during pleasant weather. Many guests describe Kupros as feeling homey and welcoming - a place where the friendly staff remembers regulars and makes newcomers feel immediately comfortable. The combination of historic architecture - quality food and drinks - and genuine community spirit has made Kupros a Midtown favorite for over a decade.
